neutral_facts.value: The accused, married to the deceased, was subjected to harassment for dowry by his family soon before her death. The deceased informed her father about the harassment, and her father and uncle took her to her parental home. The accused later took her back under threat of divorce, and she died of burn injuries. The prosecution presented evidence of the harassment, medical reports, and investigation findings. The accused denied the allegations, claiming the deceased committed suicide due to harassment by her uncle. The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court upheld the conviction but acquitted the co-accused.

key_evidence_accepted.value: There was consistent evidence on record to prove harassment for dowry soon before the death of the deceased. The deceased died within 10 months of the marriage. According to PW3, father of the deceased, after three months of the marriage, the deceased informed him that the appellant and his family were harassing her for dowry. He, along with PW-12, went to the house of the appellant and requested them not to harass her. Again, three days before the occurrence, on 28th April, 2001, the deceased informed her father about the dowry harassment on which her uncle PW-12, along with his wife, went to the house of the accused and brought the deceased to her parental home. The appellant took her away on the threat of divorce and on the next day, she died of burn injuries.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that Kashmiri Lal, Guddar Mal, and Raghubir Lal have specifically and categorically deposed about the demand of dowry soon before her death. The suicide note was not considered as an encyclopedia of the entire situation and was not sufficient to exonerate the appellant.

quotes.text: The Judgment of the Court was delivered by ADARSH KUMAR GOEL J. 1. This appeal has been preferred against Judgment and Order dated 12th March, 2013 of the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in Criminal Appeal No.S-736-SB of 2003 upholding the conviction of the appellant under Section 304-B of the Indian Penal Code ("IPC") and sentence of Rigorous Imprisonment tot seven years.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that there was consistent evidence to prove harassment for dowry by the husband soon before the death of the victim-deceased, and that the husband's actions led to the deceased's suicide by burn injuries.

quotes.text: The prosecution case is that the appellant was married to the deceased Rekha Rani on 7th July, 2000. After the marriage, she was harassed for having brought insufficient dowry and the appellant raised a demand for motor cycle apart from the demands by his mother and younger brother.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the demand of dowry 'soon before the death' and that the deceased's suicide note indicated she was not being harassed. They also claimed the appellant's case should be treated at par with his mother and brother who were acquitted.

quotes.text: The accused denied the prosecution allegations and stated that the deceased committed suicide on account of harassment by her uncle Raghubir Lal (PW-12) who wanted her to relinquish her rights in the parental property. The accused examined Vined Kumar (DW-1) who had taken the deceased to the hospital and stated that her relations with the accused were cordial.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that harassment for dowry 'soon before the death' is a necessary ingredient for the offence under Section 304-B of the IPC, and that the statutory presumption under Section 113B of the Evidence Act applies when such harassment is proven.

quotes.text: There is consistent evidence on record to prove harassment for dowry soon before the death of the deceased. The deceased died within 10 months of the marriage. According to PW3, father of the deceased, after three months of the marriage, the deceased informed him that the appellant and his family were harassing her for dowry.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because there was consistent evidence of harassment for dowry soon before the death of the deceased, and the husband's responsibility towards his wife was deemed higher than that of other relatives.

quotes.text: The husband is not only primarily responsible for safety of his wife, he is expected to be conversant with her state of mind more than any other relative. If the wife commits suicide by setting herself on fire, preceded by dissatisfaction of the husband and his family from the dowry, the inference of harassment against the husband may be patent.

other_sentence_order.value: The appellant is directed to surrender to undergo the remaining sentence, failing which he may be arrested and committed to custody to complete the sentence awarded to him.
